verdict.tagline: Cooperative submarine survival that rewards patience and teamwork under pressure.
for_you_if: you have a dedicated group for multiplayer sessions
you enjoy deep systems and complex management tasks
not_for_you_if: you prefer playing solo without a crew
you are frustrated by clunky controls and interface jank

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players appreciate the cooperative submarine mechanics, though managing AI crewmates and dealing with clunky controls or jank bring frustration.

claims.claim: Managing AI crewmates during emergency situations can cause significant progress loss due to small mistakes, requiring direct player control over them.

citations.review_text: Although much [i]Barotrauma[/i] is apparently carried by its modding community, especially after all the singleplayer (campaign) content has been explored, the game itself provides plenty of content and understandable gameplay mechanics for both leisure and hardcore playthroughs. Much of the difficulty comes from managing AI crewmates in emergency situations where the AI makes a series of small though inexcusable mistakes that can cost hours of progress, very often necessitating direct control over them to ensure no resources or members of the crew are unnecessarily expended. Other than that, with how much breathing space is provided during missions, players can explore the oceanic abyss, gather alien resources, and coherently rend colossal and human-sized creatures comparatively coherently. With this product being $35, it is recommended to get it at a 50% discount, as there are not enough mods to fix the jankiness of the base game, the user interface can be eye-strain-inducing at times, and gameplay can either be hours of going from point A to point B with little opportunities to go diving.

Incredibly difficult game in which I have not made almost any progress in yet enjoyed every second.

The solo and multiplayer experiences are incredible allowing for use a NPCs to manage differing parts of your sub while you can more effectively manage whatever you are comfortable with. Solo allowing you to swap between different NPCs makes solo feel that much better. Combined with the amazing progression, with the limited amount I have experienced, allowing immense customization of your sub while also involving, skill trees, perks, leveling system akin to Project Zomboid allowing a further interactive playthrough. The enemies are also amazing, fitting a Lovecraftian theme throughout the entire game adding layers to combat through different attacks and behaviors dependent on the enemy skyrockets the enjoyment of the game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as cumbersome and motion as clunky, making active play feel annoying or bad.

citations.review_text:
Cumbersome controls and feels bad to actively play. Great idea though, would like to see it performed better.
Maybe the clunkiness is intentional.

Mechanically rich and deep - but doesn't have a hook or tutorial that encourages exploration beyond walls of text. 

I'm fine with that for a Grand Strategy game, but combine that with QWOP motion and "artistic" visibility and it's honestly just annoying to play.

claims.claim: The game features cooperative multiplayer where players work together to manage submarine systems, repair hull damage, and fight off attacking sea creatures.

citations.review_text:
Barotrauma is one of the most immersive co-op survival games I've played. The atmosphere is incredible every mission keeps you on edge, and the feeling of exploring the dark ocean never gets old. You never know what's waiting outside the hull, which makes every trip exciting.

The survival mechanics are a real highlight. Managing the submarine, repairing damage under pressure, keeping systems running, and working together with the crew creates some genuinely tense and memorable moments. The crafting system is also well done, giving you plenty of reasons to gather resources and steadily improve your equipment without feeling overwhelming.

If you enjoy survival games that reward teamwork, exploration, and problem-solving, Barotrauma is an easy recommendation. It's challenging, atmospheric, and incredibly satisfying when your crew pulls through against the odds.

Reminds me of carrion! It's fun and simple, Of course in barotrauma you've got quite a couple jobs, security, defense,  Maintenance, and reactor operation. The reactor does have thing's you can automatically do or manually do, manage fission rates. But as i said, you could set it to automatic to manage.

To summarize it, Defend the submarine, kill the intruders, Manage the reactor, and repair systems while navigating the submarine and completing your mission.

citations.review_text:
starts getting a lot better around sea 3 but unfortunately that's also when it decides to give you frame drops so bad that you can't even defend yourself or the sub

even without lag though i just really hate the time it takes to get to the fun parts of the game and the main 2 reasons i haven't just straight up ditched the game yet are because the combat is pretty decent for the most part (when it isn't lagging like hell) and i like the lore and worldbuilding enough to want to see the ending

Barotrauma is one of my favourite co-op games. Setbacks encountered during missions require quick thinking and communication, but are not so complicated as to feel overwhelming or impossible to solve. This creates a high-stress environment that's fun to experience with friends or alone.

The game mechanics range from simple to requiring a few previous attempts to understand. For example, welding a hull can be done without experience, whilst repairing a late-game beacon station might require further instructions. However, Barotrauma scales difficulty with progression, allowing players to gradually familiarise themselves with harder tasks.

Barotrauma's visuals are okay. They fit the horror theme well, but seem a bit dark at times. I was impressed that it managed to run smoothly on decade-old laptop hardware. Performance in the late game seemed to deteriorate due to the game's single-threaded design, but this was resolved using workshop optimisation mods.

Much of my time has been spent on the single-player campaign. It was doable, but slow, as the AI needed a lot of micromanagement and constant attention. This made some missions impractical due to the time they would require to complete alone, such as exploring ruins. Playing with friends is certainly a lot more fun.

To conclude, Barotrauma is an excellent, rapid, high-adrenaline co-op game. It finds a good balance between difficulty and accessibility, whilst not giving the impression that too much is lost when missions fail. The game has enough content and difficulty progression to provide many hours of fun.
